# Current system

Outcome: teams of up to 30 people can edit shared project notes while disconnected for as long as 48 hours and reconcile later.

- C1: Desktop clients keep local state in SQLite.
- C2: The existing HTTPS sync service may be changed, but no new managed service may be introduced.
- C3: End-to-end encryption prevents the server from reading or semantically merging note content.
- C4: The audit view must preserve causally valid ordering and identify the originating device.
- C5: This task is selection only; no repository or runtime mutation is authorized.

Challengeable assumption: every note must use the same synchronization mechanism.
Must-not-challenge assumptions: C3 and C4.
fixtures.research/architecture-landscape.md:
# Offline landscape snapshot

- PA1 — Automerge: operation-based CRDT library for local-first JSON documents; close match for convergent concurrent editing, but encrypted transport and the audit projection remain application concerns.
- PA2 — Git: distributed object graph and three-way merge; close analogue for append-only history and reconciliation, but interactive note editing and conflict presentation differ.
- PA3 — Matrix event DAG: federated events carry causal references; an analogue for causally ordered audit history, not a drop-in encrypted document merge.
- PA4 — Per-field ownership queues: no close implementation was found in this bounded snapshot; only generic partitioned-work queues were found.

Scope limit: these four summaries are the complete benchmark landscape. Absence here is not proof of external absence.

constraints_preserved: C1: Desktop clients keep local state in SQLite.
C2: The existing HTTPS sync service may change, with no new managed service.
C3: End-to-end encryption prevents server semantic access or merging of note content.
C4: Audit views preserve causally valid ordering and originating-device identity.
C5: This is selection-only; no repository or runtime mutation is authorized.
variant_a.research_scope: Only the supplied current-system description and four-item offline landscape snapshot were used.
close_matches: PA1 Automerge for convergent concurrent note editing
PA3 Matrix event DAG for causally valid audit ordering
PA4 per-field ownership queues as an unresolved partitioning analogue

ideas.title: Encrypted operation-log CRDT for every note
ideas.mechanism: Each SQLite client stores encrypted, device-signed CRDT operations; the existing HTTPS service relays opaque operations, while clients materialize notes and construct the causal audit view locally.
ideas.exact_difference: Adds opaque encrypted relay, device-origin audit projection, and the existing service constraint to the CRDT pattern.

ideas.title: Encrypted immutable revision graph with client-side three-way merge
ideas.mechanism: Clients create signed encrypted revision objects with parent references, synchronize them through the existing HTTPS service, and perform three-way merges locally when note heads diverge.
ideas.exact_difference: Uses encrypted note revisions and local conflict presentation for collaborative notes rather than plaintext source trees.

ideas.title: Dual-mode notes: CRDT for collaborative notes, revision graph for deliberate notes
ideas.mechanism: A note declares its synchronization class locally: live collaborative notes use encrypted CRDT operations, while structured or low-contention notes use encrypted revision graphs and explicit local merge. Both emit one signed causal audit envelope format.
ideas.exact_difference: The synchronization mechanism varies by note while audit identity and causal ordering remain uniform; this directly rejects the one-mechanism assumption.

ideas.title: Encrypted causal envelope independent of content merge
ideas.mechanism: Every locally created mutation or revision carries an encrypted payload plus clear-to-authorized-client causal references and device signature; clients derive a causally valid audit order independently of the selected content merge engine.
ideas.exact_difference: Separates a common encrypted audit-causality layer from note-content synchronization and semantic merge.

ideas.title: Per-field ownership leases with offline intent queues
ideas.mechanism: Clients assign fields or sections temporary device ownership and queue conflicting offline intents for later owner-mediated resolution, retaining signed causal records for every attempted change.
ideas.exact_difference: Applies ownership partitioning to encrypted collaborative notes with offline reconciliation and causal audit requirements.

deepened_directions.mechanism: Encrypted operation-log CRDT for every note
deepened_directions.exact_difference: Opaque encrypted, device-signed operations are relayed by the existing HTTPS service, and audit ordering is derived client-side.
deepened_directions.benefit: Strong concurrent-edit convergence with a comparatively direct migration path from local SQLite state.
deepened_directions.load_bearing_risk: The chosen operation metadata and compaction approach may fail to preserve verifiable causal audit order without leaking unacceptable information or creating unbounded client storage.
deepened_directions.falsification: Construct a small disconnected multi-device trace with concurrent edits and compaction, then verify locally that every displayed audit entry has a valid causal predecessor relation and device origin without decrypting on the service.

deepened_directions.mechanism: Dual-mode notes with a shared encrypted causal envelope
deepened_directions.closest_match: PA1 — Automerge plus PA2 — Git, with PA3 — Matrix event DAG for audit causality
deepened_directions.exact_difference: Different notes select CRDT or revision-graph reconciliation while sharing one signed, causally linked audit representation.
deepened_directions.benefit: Challenges the uniform-sync assumption while keeping a viable CRDT path for high-collaboration notes and clearer merge semantics for deliberate notes.
deepened_directions.load_bearing_risk: A common audit envelope may not faithfully normalize causality, identity, migrations, and user-visible history across fundamentally different merge engines.
deepened_directions.falsification: Model one note of each mode with a mode migration after offline divergence, then check whether a local audit projection remains causally valid, device-attributed, and intelligible without content access by the service.

deepened_directions.mechanism: Per-field ownership leases with offline intent queues
deepened_directions.exact_difference: Ownership and queued intents are applied to encrypted note fields under long offline periods and device-origin audit requirements.
deepened_directions.benefit: Could reduce true concurrent conflicts for structured notes without requiring all content to use a CRDT.
deepened_directions.load_bearing_risk: Ownership semantics may create blocking, stale authority, or conflict escalation that is worse than deterministic merge after 48 hours offline.
deepened_directions.falsification: Simulate two devices editing the same field while each is offline under stale ownership, and determine whether deterministic local reconciliation preserves both intent and causally valid attribution.

traps: Treating encrypted relay metadata as permission for the server to semantically merge content would violate C3.
Using wall-clock order as audit order can violate C4 during 48-hour disconnection and clock skew.
A single note-wide CRDT can impose unnecessary complexity on notes that need explicit reviewable merges.
Field ownership can become unavailable or misleading after prolonged offline work, device loss, or concurrent stale ownership.
A dual-mode design can create user confusion unless mode selection, migration, and cross-mode audit semantics are explicit.

decision_point.selection_required: Choose whether to retain one universal encrypted CRDT mechanism (A1) or validate the differentiated dual-mode model with a shared causal audit envelope (A3); retain A2 as the near-current reconciliation comparator.

constraints_preserved: C1: Desktop clients retain local SQLite state.
C2: Only the existing HTTPS sync service is used; no new managed service is proposed.
C3: Server transport remains opaque and performs no semantic merge.
C4: Signed parent-referenced events preserve causally valid, device-attributable audit history.
C5: This is selection-only; no files, runtime, implementation, experiment, or durable record were changed.
variant_b.research_scope: Only the supplied current-system description and four-item landscape snapshot were used.
close_matches: PA1 Automerge for convergent text-operation editing
PA2 Git for immutable object history and reconciliation
PA3 Matrix event DAG for causal audit history
PA4 per-field ownership queues is unresolved in the supplied snapshot

ideas.title: Per-device encrypted operation logs
ideas.mechanism: Append device-signed encrypted operations and deterministically materialize locally.
ideas.exact_difference: Adds opaque HTTPS transport and a device-attributable audit projection.

ideas.title: Signed parent-referenced causal events
ideas.mechanism: Use device-key signatures and parent hashes to form the audit DAG.
ideas.exact_difference: Events are end-to-end encrypted note events, with local-only semantic interpretation.

ideas.title: Visible concurrent sibling states
ideas.mechanism: Retain concurrent heads rather than inventing a false total order.
ideas.exact_difference: Applies causal-frontier visibility to encrypted note materialization.

ideas.title: Deterministic local weaving
ideas.mechanism: Apply a device edit stream only after referenced predecessors are present.
ideas.exact_difference: Combines operation eligibility with explicit device-stream audit rules.

ideas.title: Adaptive encrypted sync profiles
ideas.mechanism: Select delta, immutable-segment, or encrypted-block replication per note.
ideas.exact_difference: A single encrypted audit envelope spans deliberately different per-note mechanisms.

ideas.title: Encrypted manifest-selected modes
ideas.mechanism: An encrypted manifest selects text-log, immutable-set, or manual-review behavior.
ideas.exact_difference: The manifest makes mode selection an auditable note property while HTTPS remains opaque.

ideas.title: Human-resolved encrypted forks
ideas.mechanism: Persist conflicting heads until a signed human resolution event joins them.
ideas.exact_difference: Forks and resolutions remain encrypted causal events with device-level attribution.

ideas.title: Independently clocked encrypted lanes
ideas.mechanism: Partition projects into encrypted lanes with signed cross-lane dependencies.
ideas.exact_difference: Introduces independently clocked note lanes and cross-lane dependency records.

ideas.title: Fixed-frame encrypted write-ahead log
ideas.mechanism: Exchange durable encrypted frame ranges with SQLite-backed checkpoints.
ideas.exact_difference: Uses fixed-size streaming frames rather than Git objects and supports resumable opaque sync.

ideas.title: Resumable encrypted segment exchange
ideas.mechanism: Use durable outboxes, idempotent receipts, and encrypted segment ranges.
ideas.exact_difference: Targets intermittent HTTPS reconciliation without server merge authority.

ideas.title: Immutable encrypted fragments
ideas.mechanism: Replicate encrypted fragments independently through signed parent references.
ideas.closest_match: PA2 Git and PA3 Matrix event DAG
ideas.exact_difference: Combines object-like fragments with causal device audit.

ideas.title: Opaque reconciliation mailbox
ideas.mechanism: Use existing HTTPS as an encrypted capsule relay keyed to frontier identifiers.
ideas.exact_difference: Uses deterministic recipient-side buffering rather than federated event routing.

ideas.title: Acknowledgement-guided encrypted gossip
ideas.mechanism: Use client-side acknowledgement history to prioritize opaque envelope exchange.
ideas.exact_difference: Treats acknowledgements as local delivery heuristics, not server-visible semantics.

ideas.title: Rotating device replica rings
ideas.mechanism: Assign encrypted note regions to changing client replica groups.
ideas.exact_difference: Uses rotating replication membership rather than a queue, but no close supplied match exists.

deepened_directions.mechanism: Manifest-selected sync modes with a common signed causal envelope
deepened_directions.closest_match: PA1 Automerge for text, PA2 Git for immutable objects, and PA3 Matrix event DAG for audit
deepened_directions.exact_difference: A per-note encrypted manifest selects the merge model while every mode emits the same device-signed parent-referenced envelope over opaque HTTPS.
deepened_directions.benefit: Matches sync behavior to note shape without weakening C1-C4 or introducing a service.
deepened_directions.load_bearing_risk: Parent rules, device sequence rules, and cross-mode conversion may yield signed but causally ambiguous histories.
deepened_directions.falsification: Do not run it now; later, validate a paper/schema trace containing concurrent offline events, missing parents, duplicate sequences, and an attempted cross-mode import.

deepened_directions.closest_match: PA2 Git three-way reconciliation and PA3 Matrix event DAG
deepened_directions.exact_difference: Conflicting note heads remain encrypted, locally materialized causal branches until a human-authored resolution event selects a successor.
deepened_directions.benefit: Avoids pretending all content is safely auto-mergeable; preserves provenance and makes conflict policy visible.
deepened_directions.load_bearing_risk: Offline device authorization, revocation, and resolver authority must be causally auditable or removed devices can produce apparently valid resolutions.
deepened_directions.falsification: Do not run it now; later, model a revoked offline device issuing a branch and resolution, then check whether all clients reject it at the correct causal point.

deepened_directions.mechanism: Adaptive encrypted sync profiles with auditable migration bridges
deepened_directions.exact_difference: Profile declaration and a signed bridge preserve one audit chain while switching between delta and immutable-segment mechanics.
deepened_directions.benefit: Offers a migration path from a near-current text CRDT architecture while reducing cost for large or attachment-heavy notes.
deepened_directions.load_bearing_risk: A checkpoint or migration bridge can sever provenance or change interpretation of historical edits.
deepened_directions.falsification: Do not run it now; later, construct a signed delta-to-segment bridge and verify that every pre-bridge causal head and device attribution remains reconstructible.

traps.reason: Reserved clock ranges do not establish cross-device causality and add fragile ordering machinery.
Cross-lane dependencies create a second distributed-consistency problem.
Replica-ring membership and recovery add an unnecessary distributed layer.
Streaming reconciliation is useful substrate but does not challenge the uniform-mechanism assumption.

decision_point.selection_required: Choose whether product policy favors manifest-selected modes (I4), explicit human-resolved forks (A6), or a near-current universal encrypted CRDT/event-log comparator (I1).

Ziel: Kontextwechsel im achtköpfigen Support-Team reduzieren, ohne Kundenkommunikation zu automatisieren.

- K1: Antworten werden ausschließlich von Menschen versendet.
- K2: Das bestehende Ticketsystem bleibt der einzige dauerhafte Datenspeicher.

# Begrenzte Workflow-Landschaft

- L1: Klassische Skill-based Routing Queues weisen Tickets nach Thema zu.
- L2: WIP-begrenzte Kanban-Pull-Systeme reduzieren parallele Arbeit.
- L3: Batched Triage bündelt Klassifikation in festen Zeitfenstern.
- L4: Assistenzsysteme schlagen Antworten vor; das ist wegen K1 nur als Vorbereitung, nicht als Versandmechanismus passend.

Recherchegrenze: ausschließlich L1 bis L4; keine Aussage über vollständige Marktneuheit.

constraints_preserved: K2: Das bestehende Ticketsystem bleibt einziger dauerhafter Datenspeicher.
K3: Jede Empfehlung nennt ihr auslösendes Ticket-Signal.
K4: Jede Shortlist-Richtung ist als Auswahlansicht oder ticket-native Empfehlung binnen zwei Wochen mit vorhandenen Integrationen prüfbar.
K5: Es wurden nur Optionen entwickelt; nichts geändert oder implementiert.
variant_a.research_scope: Die Einordnung vergleicht ausschließlich mit L1–L4 und belegt keine vollständige Marktneuheit.

ideas.title: Konflikt-Eskalationsansicht
ideas.mechanism: Zeigt nur Tickets mit mehrfachen Besitzansprüchen oder rückgängig gemachter Zuweisung; Menschen wählen die nächste Übernahme.
ideas.exact_difference: Auswahl nach nachweisbarem Übergabekonflikt statt Themenzuweisung.

ideas.title: Prüfhinweis für Risikofälle
ideas.mechanism: Markiert Ticketentwürfe mit definierten Risikosignalen für menschliche Prüfung.
ideas.exact_difference: Prüf-Auswahl statt Antwortvorschlag.

ideas.title: Ticket-native Ablehnungsgründe
ideas.mechanism: Erfasst die menschliche Ablehnung einer Routing-Empfehlung mit strukturiertem Grund im Ticket.
ideas.exact_difference: Nutzt Ablehnungsfeedback als erklärbare Auswahlgrundlage.

ideas.title: Übergabeakte im Ticket
ideas.mechanism: Standardisierte Ticketnotiz dokumentiert Kontext, Verantwortungsgrenze und Übergabesignal.
ideas.exact_difference: Kontextkompression bei menschlicher Übergabe.

ideas.title: Vier-Augen-Auswahl bei Datenkonflikt
ideas.mechanism: Fälle mit widersprüchlichen Pflichtdaten werden zur menschlichen Zweitprüfung ausgewählt.
ideas.exact_difference: Datensignal löst Auswahl aus, keine Antwortassistenz.

ideas.title: Kontextschutz für Prüffälle
ideas.mechanism: Kennzeichnet aktive prüfkritische Bearbeitung, damit neue Fälle nicht bevorzugt zugestellt werden.
ideas.exact_difference: Unterbrechungsschutz statt allgemeiner WIP-Grenze.

ideas.title: Thematische Lieferwellen
ideas.mechanism: Bündelt neue Tickets zeitlich und stellt sie als thematische Pakete bereit.
ideas.exact_difference: Kombiniert feste Triagefenster mit thematischen Arbeitswellen.

ideas.title: Rücklauf-Pool
ideas.mechanism: Wählt nach Kundeneingang zurückkehrende Tickets für einen kleinen Wiedervorlage-Pool aus.
ideas.exact_difference: Rücklaufereignis statt Thema als Auswahlsignal.

ideas.title: Last-Mile-Tisch
ideas.mechanism: Wählt Tickets mit intern hinterlegter Lösung für menschliche Finalisierung aus.
ideas.exact_difference: Verbindet Fachklärung und menschlichen Abschluss in getrennten Rollen.

ideas.title: Milk-Run-Pakete
ideas.mechanism: Stellt Personen zu festen Zeiten passende Ticketpakete bereit.
ideas.exact_difference: Pull-Pakete pro Person statt zentraler Klassifikationsbatches.

ideas.title: Human-in-the-loop Cross-Dock
ideas.mechanism: Empfiehlt bei eindeutigem Ticketfeld eine Fachqueue; der Mensch akzeptiert, ändert oder ignoriert sie.
ideas.exact_difference: Eindeutige Feldregel als sichtbare Empfehlung statt automatische Zuweisung.

ideas.title: Vorfalls-Container
ideas.mechanism: Bündelt Tickets mit gleichem Fehlercode oder Vorfall in einer temporären Arbeitsladung.
ideas.exact_difference: Vorfallssignale bündeln Recherchearbeit bei einzelnen menschlichen Antworten.

ideas.title: Rotierende Schicht-Patenschaft
ideas.mechanism: Schichten betreuen Segmente; Übergaben innerhalb der Schicht bleiben möglich.
ideas.exact_difference: Zeitlich begrenzte Segmentverantwortung statt dauerhafter Ticketbesitz.

ideas.title: Freiwilliger Übernahme-Pool
ideas.mechanism: Zeigt übernahmefähigen Personen nur Fälle mit Offline- oder Fachwechsel-Signal.
ideas.exact_difference: Pull durch freiwillige Übernahme nach erklärbarem Verfügbarkeitssignal.

ideas.title: Themenfenster
ideas.mechanism: Menschen ziehen außerhalb von Eskalationen nur Tickets eines aktuellen Themas.
ideas.exact_difference: Bearbeitungsfenster statt bloßer Klassifikationsfenster.

ideas.title: Schichtende-Übergabemarktplatz
ideas.mechanism: Offene Fälle werden mit Kontext angeboten und aktiv von Kolleg:innen ausgewählt.
ideas.exact_difference: Aktive menschliche Übernahme statt Queue-Pull.

ideas.title: Komplexitätsbudget
ideas.mechanism: Empfiehlt nur Tickets eines bereits aktiven Falltyps, wenn die Typenvielfalt hoch ist.
ideas.exact_difference: WIP wird als Themenvielfalt statt Ticketanzahl gemessen.

ideas.title: Kundenfokus-Arbeitsgruppe
ideas.mechanism: Bündelt wiederkehrende Kontakte eines Kunden für eine Schicht ohne Datenkopie.
ideas.exact_difference: Kundenhistorie statt Thema als Bündelungssignal.

deepened_directions.load_bearing_risk: Mehrere Felder können widersprüchliche Fachqueues nahelegen.
Vage oder uneinheitliche Gründe erzeugen irreführende Muster.

shortlist.why: Direkt gegen kostspielige Kontextwechsel durch fehlgeschlagene Übergaben; Ticketereignisse liefern die Erklärung.
Eng begrenzte, nachvollziehbare Fachauswahl mit menschlicher Endentscheidung; in zwei Wochen als Ansicht oder Empfehlung prüfbar.
Macht menschliche Korrekturen zur erklärbaren Lernspur, ohne neuen Speicher oder Auto-Routing.

traps.reason: Können zu verzögernden Prozesssperren werden und den Prototypumfang überschreiten.
Feste Fenster gefährden dringliche Fälle und liegen nah an L3.
Ohne eindeutiges Ticketfeld und menschlichen Rückweg entstehen unklare Zuständigkeiten.
Stark verhaltens- und staffingabhängig; in zwei Wochen schwer belastbar prüfbar.
Nur zulässig, wenn Grund im Ticket selbst gespeichert wird.

decision_point.status: Auswahl aus R1, L5 oder R3 erforderlich

# System

A coordinator consumes worker events from an in-process queue, persists checkpoints in SQLite, and publishes progress over a WebSocket. Workers await coordinator acknowledgement before requesting new work. A watchdog observes progress messages but not queue depth.

Offline analogue notes: lost wakeups, acknowledgement cycles, blocking SQLite transactions, and progress-observer failure are established failure classes. The observations do not distinguish them.

ideas.mechanism: A lost queue wakeup leaves the coordinator asleep after a worker emits worker.completed; the completion remains unconsumed or its availability is not re-signalled.
ideas.exact_difference: The supplied system uses an in-process worker-event queue and worker.completed is the recurrent terminal visible event.

ideas.mechanism: A circular acknowledgement dependency occurs: a worker waits for coordinator acknowledgement before new work, while the coordinator waits for an event or state transition that requires that worker to proceed.
ideas.exact_difference: Here the documented worker policy explicitly gates further work on coordinator acknowledgement.
ideas.search_scope: Offline analogue notes in debug/system.md only
ideas.falsification: For one reproduction, capture the existing protocol state at stall: last completion sent, acknowledgement issued, and each worker's await reason. Absence of any outstanding acknowledgement wait falsifies the cycle.

ideas.mechanism: A SQLite checkpoint transaction blocks coordinator progress after completion handling, preventing acknowledgement and new dispatch without exhausting memory or disk.

ideas.title: Persisted export job with polling
ideas.mechanism: POST creates an export-job record and returns its identifier; a worker generates the file and clients poll job status until a signed download URL is ready.

ideas.title: Export inbox with callback delivery
ideas.mechanism: Create a durable export request, process it asynchronously, then notify a registered webhook or in-app notification when the artifact is ready.

ideas.title: Streaming snapshot handoff
ideas.mechanism: Accept the request synchronously only long enough to create a consistent dataset snapshot, then hand the snapshot reference to a worker that streams the artifact to storage.

ideas.title: Fan-out shard exports with manifest assembly
ideas.mechanism: Split large exports into deterministic partitions, process shards in parallel, then publish a manifest and assembled artifact when all partitions succeed.

ideas.title: Priority-aware export scheduler
ideas.mechanism: Route exports through a scheduler with quotas, deduplication, cancellation, and priority classes; workers consume only admitted jobs.

ideas.title: Reusable materialized export views
ideas.mechanism: Continuously build approved export projections so requests mostly package a ready projection rather than query and transform live source data.

shortlist.why: It cleanly removes request-time work, supports retries and cancellation, gives clients explicit progress, and is the smallest dependable foundation for later notification or scheduling enhancements.
It strengthens consistency and retry behavior where exports traverse mutable or expensive source data, but adds snapshot lifecycle complexity.
It protects shared capacity and improves fairness, but is most valuable after the durable job boundary exists.

traps.trap: Returning a download URL before artifact durability is confirmed
traps.mitigation: Publish readiness only after storage write and integrity checks complete.

traps.trap: Retrying a job against changed live data
traps.mitigation: Persist immutable request parameters and a snapshot/version reference.

traps.trap: Duplicate submissions creating duplicate costly exports
traps.mitigation: Use an idempotency key and request fingerprint.
Set explicit expiry, deletion, and client-visible expiration semantics.
Keep the status endpoint authoritative and make notifications best-effort or durably retried.

decision_point.stop_reason: The strongest current recommendation is the persisted export job with polling, but implementation authority transfers only after a human explicitly selects a direction; therefore no changes were made.
